- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.00) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days) are common; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If 30-day forecast shows consistent upward trend but true outcome shows mean reversion within 10–15 days, reduce slope of forecast by 10–20%.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model often misjudges turning points; use sentiment swing as trigger for early correction.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid overfitting to recent 18-day history; if forecast is >10% above 18-day mean, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports it.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast for 5+ days, consider “price floor” effect — model may be ignoring supply/demand constraints; reduce forecast by 2–5% per day until convergence.
